chunks: You have said a lot about the killers of Uthman. You first join what the people have joined (i.e., allegiance), then seek a verdict about (the accused people) from me, and I shall settle the matter between you and them according to the Book of Allah, the Sublime. But what you are aiming at is just the fake nipple given to a child in the first days of stopping of nursing. Peace be on those who deserve it.

key_terms.خُدْعَةُ الصَّبِيِّ: Deception of the child / Fake nipple

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the 'fake nipple' metaphor in Ali's response to Muawiya regarding Uthman's killers?
ai.summary: Ali (peace be upon him) invites Muawiya to set aside the specific grievance of Uthman's killers and submit to his arbitration, framing the demand for retribution as a pretext for political consolidation. The metaphor of the 'fake nipple' (khud'at al-sabi) highlights how Muawiya’s claim to justice was merely a deceptive lure to draw the people into a power struggle rather than a genuine pursuit of divine law. This exchange underscores the Shia scholarly view of the conflict as a struggle between legitimate authority and opportunistic ambition, rooted in the Quranic principle of returning disputes to God and the Prophets.
